note: Exhaustive ground-truth manifest for the Maple House governance tension bench. Sections keyed by Charter article numeral or Decision date (both unique). Every genuine cross-section conflict is labeled as a planted tension; every superficially-related-but-compatible pair is labeled expected_non. Splits: train (tunable), dev (tunable), test (sacred — PeekBudget guards it). NOT shipped into the corpus.

planted_tensions.why: Charter permits overnight guests up to two nights; the decision forbids overnight guests entirely.
Charter bans all pets except fish; the decision allows a house cat.
Charter forbids reserving a common area for exclusive use; the decision lets a member reserve the dining room.
Charter sets quiet hours from 11 PM; the Thursday movie night runs until midnight.
Charter sets quiet hours at 11 PM; the decision silently moves the weeknight start to 10 PM.
Charter requires whoever used the kitchen to clean it; the decision exempts the cook (unmarked exception to the rule).
Charter states no member is exempt from chores; the decision exempts long-traveling members.
Charter states no member is exempt from chores for any reason; excusing the cook from kitchen cleanup is a chore exemption (this decision conflicts with BOTH Art III and Art V).

Article IV forbids reserving a common area for exclusive use and requires it stay open to all; Article XI reserves the dining room for silent study every weeknight 7-9 PM. Two charter articles in conflict.
Weeknight quiet hours (Sun-Thu) begin at 10 PM; the Thursday movie night may run until midnight. Thursday after 10 PM is governed by both — ambiguous scope.

Article XI reserves the dining room for silent study every weeknight 7-9 PM; the 2026-05-06 decision lets a member reserve the dining room for a private event. A booking during the study window conflicts — both claim the dining room exclusively. Detector-surfaced gap (like T8).

expected_non_tensions.why: decoy: shares vocabulary (guests, overnight) but governs car parking, not whether/how long guests stay
compatible: a sign-in logbook is an additive requirement, not a conflict with the stay limit
compatible: extends quiet hours to the backyard at the same times
compatible: indoors stays banned; the porch is outdoors
compatible: a late fee implements the existing due date
compatible: labeling fridge food is an additive kitchen rule, not a conflict with cleanup duty
compatible: two refinements of quiet hours (earlier weeknight start; backyard scope) that do not conflict
